fmt/Jack_PlugOneSwitchIntoThe2: Plug one switch into the bottom jack and it arrives as digital_in_1. Only a splitter uses digital_in_2 as well.
fmt/Jack_TheMiddleJackIsThe: The middle jack is the lip switch. A splitter there gives digital_in_5 and digital_in_6.
fmt/Jack_TheUSBAPortS: The USB-A port's own data pins, read as plain switches. Nothing plugs into these on the outside of the case.
fmt/Parse_BeginTheCellWithThe: Begin the cell with the sheet keyword, e.g. "Profile Name".
fmt/Parse_DeleteRowsAboveTheFirst: Delete rows above the first sheet header.
fmt/Parse_FirstCellMustContainProfile: First cell must contain "Profile" or be "Preferences" or "Infrared". Found "{0}".
fmt/Parse_KeepANoteOnA: Keep a note on a single line.
fmt/Parse_KeepLettersNumbersSpacesAnd: Keep letters, numbers, spaces, and "_ . -" only, or move the text to the notes column.
fmt/Parse_MoveItAboveTheFirst: Move it above the first blank row or delete it.
fmt/Parse_RawA1DoesNotSTARTWith: "{0}" does not START with "Profile", "Preferences" or "Infrared" (capitalized exactly), so the device skips this whole sheet.
fmt/Parse_RowR1AppearsAfter: Row {0} appears after a blank row, where the device stops reading this mode, so this row does nothing.
fmt/Parse_RowR1HasA: Row {0} has a cell holding more than one line. The device reads each line as a separate row, and a blank line among them stops it reading the rest of this mode, so saving joins them into one line.
fmt/Parse_RowR1IsLonger: Row {0} is longer than {1} characters including comments. The device reads a row into a 1024-byte buffer and hands back the overflow as if it were the next row. Depending on where the row happens to break, that can end the mode early and drop every row below it.
fmt/Parse_SectionStarts0ScanFromRowS: {0} row(s) before the first sheet keyword are not part of any sheet.
fmt/Parse_SetCellA1ToThe: Set cell A1 to the sheet type keyword, e.g. "Profile Name".
fmt/Parse_ShortenItTo63Characters: Shorten it to 63 characters or fewer.
fmt/Parse_ThisCellIsValueLength: This cell is {0} characters. The device stops looking for the end of a cell after 64, so it reads this cell and everything after it on this row as empty.
fmt/Parse_ValueContainsValueAtThe: "{0}" contains "{1}". The device ends a cell at that character, so it reads it as two cells ("{2}" and "{3}") and everything after it on this row moves along one column.
fmt/Sheet_CauseMissedNotReadAt: {0} {1} not read at all, so we cannot say what is in there. Split the modes you need across smaller spreadsheets and import them one at a time.
fmt/Sheet_EveryTabFromThereOn: Every tab from there on was
fmt/Sheet_TabPastTheRowCap: The tab "{0}" has cells below row {1}, far past where any profile ends, so we stopped reading that tab there and cannot say what is under it. If that is a stray cell left behind by a paste, deleting the empty rows at the bottom of the tab and importing again will clear this.
fmt/Sheet_ThatSpreadsheetHoldsAPart: That spreadsheet holds a part of {0} MB, far larger than any profile, so it was not read.
fmt/Sheet_ThisSpreadsheetHasMoreThan: This spreadsheet has more than {0} tabs, and we read the first {1}.
fmt/Sheet_WorkbookPastTheRowCap: This spreadsheet is larger than {0} rows, far larger than any profile, so we stopped reading part way through.
pref/joystick_deflection_minimum/descrip: Center dead zone for the analog stick, as a percent of full travel. Set it high enough to stop a wandering mouse or joystick. Larger numbers make the stick less sensitive around the center. This is a separate thing from the D-Pad rings. On firmware 2373 a value of 0 no longer means no dead zone: the device substitutes 129 raw counts instead, and it redoes that on every scan, so it wins over the value worked out when the file was loaded.
pref/joystick_deflection_maximum/descrip: How far the stick has to move for a full signal. QMP calls this the joystick's range of motion and it is the nearest thing the device has to a sensitivity control: larger numbers mean more travel for the same output, so the joystick feels less sensitive. QMP takes the largest of its four direction sliders.
pref/deflection_multiplier_up/descriptio: Scales the up direction so it reaches a full signal at the same point as the other directions. QMP works it out as the largest direction slider over the up one, so a larger multiplier means up reaches a full signal on less travel and feels more sensitive.
pref/deflection_multiplier_down/descript: Scales the down direction so it reaches a full signal at the same point as the other directions. QMP works it out as the largest direction slider over the down one, so a larger multiplier means down reaches a full signal on less travel and feels more sensitive.
pref/deflection_multiplier_left/descript: Scales the left direction so it reaches a full signal at the same point as the other directions. QMP works it out as the largest direction slider over the left one, so a larger multiplier means left reaches a full signal on less travel and feels more sensitive.
pref/deflection_multiplier_right/descrip: Scales the right direction so it reaches a full signal at the same point as the other directions. QMP works it out as the largest direction slider over the right one, so a larger multiplier means right reaches a full signal on less travel and feels more sensitive.
pref/joystick_D_Pad_inner/description: Percent of full deflection, measured from the center, where the inner D-Pad ring starts. It only fires after a short delay, so you can move through it on the way out without triggering it. Half this value is where a direction stops being held.
pref/joystick_D_Pad_outer/description: Percent of full deflection, measured from the center, where the outer D-Pad ring starts. Past this line a direction fires straight away.
pref/joystick_dead_zone_shape/descriptio: Use a round center dead zone instead of a square one.
pref/joystick_warning/description: Deflection past which firmware 1476 warned the user about moving the stick too far. Firmware 2373 still accepts the name but ignores it: the check is commented out.
pref/joystick_alarm/description: Deflection past which firmware 1476 sounded an alarm tone. Firmware 2373 still accepts the name but ignores it: the check is commented out.
pref/enable_auto_zero/description: Firmware 2373 ignores this. It forces the setting back to 0 after every configuration load and both places that would have read it are commented out, so turning it on changes nothing, in a mode row or on the device.
pref/sip_puff_threshold_soft/description: Pressure or vacuum level that begins a soft sip or puff.
pref/sip_puff_threshold/description: Pressure at which to trigger the output. QMP shows this as the sip and puff high threshold; sip_puff_threshold_soft is the low one.
pref/sip_puff_maximum/description: Maximum pressure to scale to a full signal.
pref/sip_puff_delay_soft/description: Soft sip and puff signals are sensed after this short delay. QMP shows this as the Low Threshold Delay.
pref/sip_puff_delay_hard/description: How long a hard sip or puff is held before it counts as a long signal. The clock starts once the hard threshold is crossed, not when the pressure first moves. 0 does not mean unset, it means the long signal fires at once.
pref/sip_threshold_soft/description: Vacuum level that begins a soft sip, since firmware 2373. At 0 the soft sip/puff threshold still applies to sips; any other value replaces it for sips only.
pref/sip_threshold/description: Vacuum level that triggers a hard sip, since firmware 2373. At 0 the hard sip/puff threshold still applies to sips; any other value replaces it for sips only.
pref/sip_maximum/description: Vacuum that scales to a full signal on a sip, since firmware 2373. At 0 the sip/puff maximum still applies to sips; any other value replaces it for sips only.
pref/puff_threshold_soft/description: Pressure that begins a soft puff, since firmware 2373. At 0 the soft sip/puff threshold still applies to puffs; any other value replaces it for puffs only.
pref/puff_threshold/description: Pressure that triggers a hard puff, since firmware 2373. At 0 the hard sip/puff threshold still applies to puffs; any other value replaces it for puffs only.
pref/puff_maximum/description: Pressure that scales to a full signal on a puff, since firmware 2373. At 0 the sip/puff maximum still applies to puffs; any other value replaces it for puffs only.
pref/enable_left_side_tube/description: Uses the left tube for mode control by swapping it with the right tube.
pref/lip_position_minimum/description: Percent lip sensor position that activates the signal.
pref/lip_position_maximum/description: Percent of lip sensor movement that gives a full signal.
